newsitem.title: USA: American pilots' board recesses talks, to resume tomorrow.
newsitem.headline: American pilots' board recesses talks, to resume tomorrow.

text.p: The American Airlines pilots union said Thursday that its board recessed meetings without taking a vote on a labour contract proposed by the nation's second largest carrier.
Meetings will resume Friday, a spokesman for the Allied Pilots Association (APA) told reporters.
"There should be a vote sometime tomorrow," said Wally Pitts, spokesman for the union, which represents 9,300 American Airlines pilots.
"The board wants to be fresh for what's expected to be a long debate tomorrow," added Brian Mayhew, chairman of the negotiating committee for the union board.
"I can't imagine there won't be a vote tomorrow," Mayhew told reporters. "They owe it to the membership to vote one way or another tomorrow."
Pitts had said the issue of who will fly smaller jets at American Airlines' regional carrier, American Eagle, remained at the centre of the meeting this afternoon.
American Airlines pilots are concerned they might lose routes to American Eagle if American Airlines buys new smaller jets for the regional subsidiary.

"The members today are trying to educate themselves on the small jet issue and that takes time," Pitts told a news conference earlier Thursday in the Chicago suburb of Arlington Heights where the meetings of the union's 18-member board are being held.
The pilots reached an agreement in principle with American last week, although the issue of who will fly small jets at the American Eagle regional division has yet to be settled.

American Airlines wants American Eagle pilots, who are paid less than APA members, to fly smaller jets so the company can remain competitive with low-cost commuter carriers. The APA pilots, however, are concerned that American Eagle pilots will eventually take over their current routes.
Under a proposed five-year deal, American pilots would receive pay increases of 9 percent and options on 5.75 million shares of AMR common stock at $10 below market price.

American Airlines also would be able to add 50- and 70-seat commuter jets at American Eagle, but the APA in return would win a guarantee that any furloughed American pilots would be moved to fly the regional commuter jets.
A two-tier B-scale pay structure also will be phased out by the end of the contract.
If the board approves the pact, it would set up a ratification vote by the rank-and-file. If the board rejects the proposal, another 30-day cooling off period would be launched.
James Sovich, president of the APA, said late Wednesday there was no indication in either direction on the board's stance on the proposal.
The APA went on strike on Feb. 15 but a Presidential Emergency Board sent pilots back to work just minutes later.
The rank-and-file has rejected board-approved agreements before. Last fall, the board accepted a proposal by American, but union members rejected it in early January.
However, rejecting the latest proposal would allow Congress to impose a contract, a prospect that some pilots have said is more onerous than any offer from American.
American Airlines is a subsidiary of AMR Corp. Shares of AMR rose $1.50 to $82.50 on the New York Stock Exchange.
